A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIT-GNN. All 17 pages of v3 and 22 pages of v4, including appendices, were readable and visually inspected. Corresponding algorithms, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original node and graph classification/regression experiments, inference timings, memory measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark experiments and adds Cora ablations, preprocessing timings, and dataset-specific computational-cost analyses.

M1.justification: The Extra Nodes and Cluster Nodes procedures, masking, losses, pooling, and Algorithms 1–5 are retained. V4 explicitly describes appended-node features and unit edge weights, but does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 13 datasets across node classification, node regression, graph classification, and graph regression, including the same four QM9 targets. New analyses reuse existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: V4 Figure 5 adds a no-appended-nodes ('None') comparator to the Cora component comparison; v3 Table 15 compared Extra Nodes and Cluster Nodes. The external comparator sets, including SGGC, GCOND, BONSAI, DOSCOND, and KIDD, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 introduces Cora setup/control comparisons, preprocessing-time measurements across coarsening ratios, and computed single-node/full-graph cost sweeps. Existing splits, training budgets, model dimensions, and timing sample counts remain unchanged. Its blanket statement that all results use variation_neighborhoods conflicts with Table 7's retained algebraic_JC setting and does not establish a universal protocol change.

E4.justification: V4 adds Cora training-setup and node-appending ablations in Figure 5 and construction-time analysis in Figure 6. Figure 4 replaces v3's schematic feasibility map with computed single-node and full-graph cost comparisons across eight datasets. Existing coarsening-algorithm ablations remain, while the explicit Chameleon Extra-versus-Cluster comparison in v3 Table 15 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations of the top ten accuracies or lowest ten MAEs for node tasks. No revised seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented. The new variance calculations in Section 4.3 concern subgraph sizes, not experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: V4 adds findings from Figures 4–6 and fills 24 previously missing QM9 entries, including GAT at r=0.7, property 0: 0.686. It omits the GIN r=0.7 ZINC result of 0.658 and the explicit Chameleon Extra Nodes results. Matched main benchmark, inference-time, and memory values remain unchanged; v3's full node-regression appendix table is simply moved into v4 Table 3.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.2 replaces the maximum-appended-node sufficient conditions with a bound involving the mean and variance of augmented subgraph sizes, supported by a new derivation. V4 adds Corollary 4.3 on feasibility of the bound. Appendix C removes v3's increasing-with-graph-size derivation and maximum-appended-node bound table, and explicitly separates single-node and full-graph cost inequalities.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: coarsening-based inference, Extra/Cluster Nodes, conditional computational advantages, competitive performance on 13 datasets, and up to approximately 100-fold inference-time and memory reductions.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands explanations of training-distribution mismatch, benefits of appended nodes, molecular positional-information loss, and preprocessing overhead. The revised complexity discussion emphasizes balanced augmented subgraphs and dataset-dependent coarsening trade-offs. It also qualifies the memory figures as storage for the graph and weight matrices.

D1.justification: V4 explicitly specifies unit edge weights and feature assignments for appended nodes, clarifies validation counts per class, and explains the scope of reported memory consumption. Appendix E's optimizer, learning rates, epochs, dimensions, hardware, and software remain unchanged, as does the embedded source-code link target.

R1.justification: V4 adds coarsening references by Joly and Keriven, Kataria et al., and Dickens et al. It also expands the explanation of how FIT-GNN differs from DOSCOND and KIDD in reducing training and test graphs. The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized language edits, expands explanations of experimental setups, introduces per-task labels in Section 6.1, updates author affiliations, and adopts author-year citations. The section sequence and Appendix A–F organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 changes typography and author layout, redesigns Table 2 with explicit split columns, and adds colored result highlighting. It brings full regression tables into the main text, reorganizes appendix tables, replaces Figure 4, and adds Figures 5–6. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond repagination.

improvement.justification: The distribution-sensitive complexity analysis, new controls, preprocessing timings, and completed QM9 entries make the efficiency argument easier to assess. These gains are tempered by removed appendix results and a new overgeneralization that all experiments use variation_neighborhoods, contrary to Table 7 and the mixed ablation findings. The central method and most benchmark evidence remain unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
